children: Copart Inc.
agreed to acquire ACV Auctions

for $10.50 a share in cash. The deal gives the digital dealer auction platform an implied equity value of about $1.9 billion. The companies announced the agreement after the market close on Thursday, alongside Copart's
fiscal fourth-quarter results.
Copart
rose 10% in extended trading Thursday, while ACV
jumped 43%.
The deal takes Copart
beyond its core salvage franchise, which is built largely on selling damaged and total-loss vehicles for insurers. ACV
gives it an immediate, scaled position in dealer-to-dealer wholesale, a channel where ACV
competes with Cox Automotive's Manheim and with Openlane
For Copart
shareholders, the question is whether a cash-funded move into clean-title used cars can open a new growth engine without denting returns. For ACV
holders, the offer delivers a defined cash exit at a sizable premium to where the stock traded before deal talk surfaced.
Deal terms
The $10.50 price is about 45% above ACV's

unaffected close on August 10. That was the last trading day before media reports of a possible transaction. The price is also about 41% above ACV's 30-day volume-weighted average through September 9.
A Copart
subsidiary will launch a tender offer for all ACV

shares. The offer requires a majority of outstanding shares to be tendered. It also needs the Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust waiting period to expire or end, plus other customary conditions. After the tender closes, remaining shares will be converted into the right to receive the same $10.50 in cash.
Copart
will fund the purchase with cash on hand. There is no financing condition. Both boards approved the deal unanimously, and the companies expect it to close by the end of calendar 2026.
Earnings impact
Copart
expects the acquisition to accelerate revenue growth. It forecasts the deal will be neutral to earnings per share in the first full year of ownership and accretive in fiscal 2028 and beyond.

The company pointed to near-term cost and revenue synergies across dealer, commercial and retail channels. It did not put a dollar figure on those synergies in the announcement. Copart said it will retain enough balance sheet flexibility to keep pursuing organic and acquisition-driven investments.
Strategic case
Copart
is pitching the combination as a fully digital remarketing platform covering a vehicle's whole life. That spans dealer trade-ins, wholesale remarketing, salvage disposition and international resale.
Copart

brings a global buyer base and more than 250 physical locations. ACV adds a commercial wholesale platform, a national network of buyers and inspectors and dealer-focused data tools. Those include inspection technology, vehicle condition data and AI-powered valuation. The companies say the combined condition dataset will rank among the largest in the industry.
Management also flagged cross-selling of buyers and sellers between the two marketplaces. It sees room to expand transportation services and commercial vehicle operations.
Copart

CEO Jay Adair called the deal a significant milestone in the company's growth strategy. He said ACV fits Copart's push into domestic whole-car sales and technology-enabled services. "Copart has strong momentum, and this acquisition fits squarely within our growth pillars," Adair said.
ACV

CEO George Chamoun said the tie-up will let ACV expand faster and innovate with global scale. He highlighted access to Copart's nationwide footprint and "a combined demand engine that ensures the right vehicle gets to the right buyer."
After closing, ACV
will run as an independent Copart
subsidiary. Its existing leadership team will stay in place.

The Hart-Scott-Rodino review is the main regulatory hurdle. Investors will also track the tender offer timeline and any synergy targets Copart shares on its conference call. The call is set for 5:30 p.m. Eastern Time today, with a webcast and slides on Copart's investor relations site.

title: Copart to buy ACV for $1.9B in cash, pushing into dealer wholesale auctions
